name: develop
description: plan -> implement (tests first) -> parallel review + test -> fix loop -> supervise. Modelled on takt's development-core / terraform workflows: agents do the work, this file decides what happens next.

rules.description: A decision that belongs to the user (requirement conflict, apply-time facts, missing access)
The task cannot be done safely within this repository's policies

plan.instruction: Investigate the request against the code and docs/. Produce plan.md per the planner output contract: requirements, so that, affected files, test-first strategy, verification commands, risks, unverified facts.

rules.description: Plan is complete and within scope

implement.instruction: Follow plan.md. Write or update the failing test first, then the change, then run .claude/scripts/verify.sh --level full. Do not commit.

rules.description: Change done and verify.sh reports PASS (or UNVERIFIED with the missing tool named)
The plan is wrong or incomplete; say why

reviewers.instruction: Each reviewer reads plan.md, implementation.md and the diff (git diff against the merge-base), and returns its report per its output contract. Reviewers never edit files.

fix.instruction: Fix every blocking finding from the latest review reports (and nothing else), then run .claude/scripts/verify.sh --level full. Answer each finding: fixed (how) or not fixed (why).

supervise.instruction: Final gate. Check every requirement in plan.md against the diff and fresh verify.sh output. Do not review style. Issue the verdict: approve, reject (with the unmet requirement) or blocked (verification impossible in this environment).

judge.instruction: The review -> fix cycle has repeated {cycle_count} times. Compare the review reports across cycles: are blocking findings shrinking and not reappearing (converging), or oscillating / conflicting (unproductive)?
